hypotheses.justification: The completeness of `E` is implied by the other hypotheses in scope: `E` has `[NormedAddCommGroup E]`, `[NormedSpace ℂ E]` (from `[InnerProductSpace ℂ E]`) and `[FiniteDimensional ℂ E]`, and `ℂ` is complete, so `FiniteDimensional.complete ℂ E : CompleteSpace E` (Mathlib, `Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/FiniteDimension.lean`, line 509: `theorem FiniteDimensional.complete [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] : CompleteSpace E`, under `[NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [CompleteSpace 𝕜]`, `[Module 𝕜 E]`, `[ContinuousSMul 𝕜 E]`, `[IsUniformAddGroup E]`, `[T2Space E]`) applies. The statement itself never needs completeness: `Lp E 2 μ`, its coercion to `α → E`, `StronglyMeasurable`, and the Bochner integrals into `E` and into `Lp E 2 μ` are all available with only `[NormedAddCommGroup E]`. In the proof the only places `CompleteSpace E` is used are the two applications of `integral_inner` (lines 266 and 280), whose hypotheses are `[CompleteSpace E]` and `[NormedSpace ℝ E]`; adding `haveI : CompleteSpace E := FiniteDimensional.complete ℂ E` at the start makes the proof go through verbatim. So the theorem remains true and provable with this argument deleted (e.g. via `omit [CompleteSpace E] in`), the rest of the statement and proof unchanged. Note `[FiniteDimensional ℂ E]` itself cannot be dropped this way: the proof uses `stdOrthonormalBasis ℂ E` and `sum_repr'`, and the available Mathlib lemma for the final step (`MeasureTheory.ae_eq_zero_of_forall_inner`) additionally requires `[SecondCountableTopology E]`, so a genuinely different argument would be needed.
